definition: Recognizing responses that push back against hateful or harmful content with constructive replies.
details: Recognizing responses that push back against hateful or harmful content with constructive replies. Identifying counterspeech helps platforms amplify it and informs automated response generation.

explainer.lead: Counterspeech detection is the task of spotting replies that answer hateful or harmful content constructively. It can help platforms amplify useful pushback and guide systems that generate responses.

tiers.eli5: Imagine someone posts a mean message, and another person replies by calmly standing up for the people being attacked. Counterspeech detection is like a helper noticing that this reply pushes back without adding more meanness. That makes it easier to show the helpful reply to more people.
tiers.practitioner: Treat detection as a reply-level classification task, with the original harmful content available as context. A counterspeech/not-counterspeech output can support ranking for amplification or inform automated response generation. Key pitfalls include confusing hostile rebuttals with constructive pushback and judging a reply without the content it answers.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a hateful or harmful post p and a candidate reply r, the task is f(p, r) -> {counterspeech, not counterspeech}. A positive label requires r both to push back against p and to do so constructively. Detection supports amplification and automated response generation; opposition alone does not satisfy the label.

explainer.example: A post says, “People from this group do not belong here.” The reply, “Everyone deserves to feel welcome; we can disagree without attacking people,” is detected as counterspeech because it rejects the exclusionary message constructively.

usedIn.name: Online content platforms
usedIn.detail: Identify constructive pushback against hateful or harmful posts so it can be amplified.

usedIn.name: Automated response generation
usedIn.detail: Use detected counterspeech to inform systems that produce constructive replies.

explainer.intuition: Not every disagreement is counterspeech: the reply must resist harmful content while remaining constructive. Detection looks for that combination rather than simply finding anger, conflict, or another hateful message.
howItWorks: Start with a reply to hateful or harmful content.
Check whether the reply pushes back against that content.
Check whether its response is constructive rather than abusive.
Label qualifying replies for amplification or response-generation use.
explainer.whyItMatters: Constructive replies can otherwise be lost among hostile exchanges. Detecting them gives platforms a way to amplify useful responses and provides a basis for better automated replies.
misconceptions: Any reply to hate speech counts as counterspeech.
Counterspeech detection is the same as hate-speech detection.
Detecting counterspeech automatically generates a reply.
